questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India declared that the Parliament has the power to abridge or take away any of the Fundamental Rights under Article 368 and such an Act, will **NOT **be a law under the meaning of Article 13?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Twenty-fourth Amendment.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Twenty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution of India, officially known as The Constitution (Twenty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1971, enables Parliament to dilute Fundamental Rights through Amendments of the Constitution.**
 
• **It also amended Article 368 to provide expressly that Parliament has the power to amend any provision of the Constitution.**
 
• **The 24th Amendment modified Articles 13 and 368 to authorize Parliament to freely amend the Fundamental Rights. **
 
 
• **Article 13 stated that any law which was inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights was invalid.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **In the Golak Nath case, the Supreme Court ruled that the word ‘law’ **also included constitutional amendments; **as a result, any constitutional amendment which violated the Fundamental Rights was invalid.**
 
• So** Parliament** would not be able to use **constitutional amendments to curtail the Fundamental Rights.**
 
• The** 24th Amendment inserted clause (4)** to Article 13,** which stated that Article 13 would not apply to any constitutional amendments, effectively overturning Golak Nath. **
 
• Article 368 lays down the procedure to amend the Constitution.
 
• **Under the original Constitution,** any constitutional amendment would only come into force if two conditions were met:
 
 
• first, if two-thirds of the members of each House of Parliament voted in its favour; 
 
• second if it received the assent of the President, who had the option of withholding assent. 
 
 
 
• **The Amendment modified the second condition, to provide that the President was bound to give his assent to the Bill - they had no choice.** 
 
• The 24th Amendment was partially overturned in 1973 when the Supreme Court held in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala that Parliament could not amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.
 
• In this case, 11 judges held that certain basic or essential features of the Constitution were beyond the scope of Parliament’s amending powers. 
 
• **Both Articles 13 and 368 continue to exist in their amended form. However, through various causes, the Courts have strived to not allow these Articles to undermine the basic structure of the Constitution. **

questions.question: Which of the following crops is described as – ‘It is a crop which is used both as food and fodder. It is a Kharif crop that requires temperature between 21°C to 27°C and grows well in old alluvial soil’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maize**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Maize is a crop that is used both as food and fodder.

 
 
• It is a Kharif crop that requires a temperature between 21°C to 27°C and grows well in old alluvial soil.
 
• In some states like Bihar maize is grown in the rabi season also.
 
• The use of modern inputs such as HYV seeds, fertilisers and irrigation have contributed to the increasing production of maize.
 
• Major maize-producing states are Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kharif Crops: Paddy, Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Arhar(Tur), Moong, Urad, Cotton, Groundnut, Sunflower Seed, Soybean Black, Sesamum, Nigerseed.
 
• Rabi crops: Wheat, Barley, Masur (Lentil), Rapeseed/Mustard, Safflower, Toria.
 
• Other Crops: Copra, De-Husked Coconut, Jute, Sugarcane.

questions.question: During the rule of which of the following dynasties did Timur or Tamerlane invade India in 1398 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Tughlaq dynasty.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Tamerlane or Timur marched into India with his army and reached Delhi in the year 1398. 
 
• Attacking the Delhi Sultanate ruled by Sultan **Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq.**
 
• He started his journey from Samarkand. After crossing the Sindh river, he entered Punjab.
 
• He crossed Indus and captured Multan, and just walked over to Delhi without much resistance.
 
• **Hence Tughlaq dynasty is the answer.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Five dynasties ruled over the Delhi Sultanate sequentially:

 
 
• Mamluk dynasty (1206–1290)
 
• Khalji dynasty (1290–1320)
 
• Tughlaq dynasty (1320–1414)
 
• Sayyid dynasty (1414–1451)
 
• Lodi dynasty (1451–1526)

questions.question: Approximately how much percentage (nearest to integer) of total water on the surface of earth is accounted for by the oceans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**97.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• 97 percent (nearest to integer) of the total water on the surface of the earth is accounted for by the oceans.

 
• Earth is called the "Blue Planet" because it looks blue from space due to the presence of water on its surface.
 
• Around 71% of the Earth's surface is covered with water.
 
• While the other 29% consists of continents and islands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Total water on earth is majorly divided into two parts:
 
 
• Freshwater (2.5%)
 
• Saline water (97.4%)
 
 
 
• Freshwater is again divided into four parts:
 
 
• Icecaps and glaciers (68.7%)
 
• Groundwater (30.1%)
 
• Surface water (0.3%) (lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, etc.)
 
• Others (0.9%) (soil moisture, atmospheric moisture, etc.)

questions.question: The foul smell from a body specially during a sultry summer is due to the action of ________ on sweat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteria.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The foul smell from a body especially during a sultry summer is due to the action of **bacteria on sweat.**

 
• Sweat glands are small tubular structures of the skin that produce sweat.
 
• Sweat glands are used to regulate temperature and remove waste by secreting water, sodium salts, and nitrogenous waste (such as urea) onto the skin surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Human sweat contains Lactic acid.
 
• Sweat contains water, minerals, lactate, and urea.
 
• Sweating is produced by sweat glands. There are two to four million sweat glands distributed all over our bodies.

questions.question: Who among the following was the ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhruva​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Main points__

 
• Rulers of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
• Dhruva (c. 780−793 CE)
 
 
• During his reign, the kingdom expanded into an empire that included all the territory between the Kaveri River and central India.
 
 
 
• Govind III (c.793−814 CE)
 
 
• It was Dhruvaputra who took the Rashtrakutas to greater heights. He became the winner in the tripartite struggle.
 
 
 
• Amoghavarsha I (c.814−878 CE)
 
 
• The most famous of the Rashtrakutas, he built the new capital city of Manyakheta (modern Malkhed).
 
• He defeated the invading Eastern Chalukyas at Vingavalli and earned the title Veeranarayana.
 
 
 
• Krishna III (c.939−967 CE) 
 
 
• The last great Rashtrakuta ruler, consolidated the empire so that it extended from the Narmada river to the Kaveri river and included the northern Tamil country (Thondaimandalam) and paid tribute to the king of Ceylon.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases can't be prevented by vaccination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beri beri.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Beriberi is easily** treated with thiamine supplements**. Hence,** do not need a vaccine.**
 
• The doctor may **prescribe a thiamine shot or pill**. For severe cases, a healthcare professional will administer **intravenous thiamine.**
 
• **Beri-beri **refers to a deficiency** of thiamine pyrophosphate**, the biologically active form of the** vitamin known as thiamine or vitamin B-1.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Measles**

 
 
• Measles is an acute viral respiratory illness.
 
• It's symptoms include:
 
 
• Fever (as high as 105°F) and malaise, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis -the three “C”s -, pathognomonic enanthema (Koplik spots) followed by a maculopapular rash.
 
• The rash usually appears about 14 days after a person is exposed.
 
 
 
• Measles can be** prevented with the MMR vaccine.​**
 
 
 
• **Typhoid**
 
 
• ​Typhoid fever is** a bacterial infection** that can spread throughout the body, affecting many organs.
 
• It's caused by a **bacterium called Salmonella typhi.**
 
• **Parenteral Vi polysaccharide and oral Ty21a** are both acceptable forms of typhoid vaccine.
 
 
 
• **Rabies**
 
 
• ​Rabies is a fatal but preventable **viral disease.**
 
• It can spread to people and pets if they are bitten or scratched by **rabid animals like bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes.**
 
• **The rabies vaccine is an active immunizing agent** used to prevent infection caused by the rabies virus.

questions.question: Who among the following first argued that in the face of high deficits, people save more?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**David Ricardo.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Ricardo** first argued in the face of high deficits, people save more.
 
• The** law of comparative advantage** is popularly attributed to English political economist David Ricardo.
 
• His book **“On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation” was **written in 1817.
 
• Comparative advantage is an economy's ability to produce a particular good or service at a lower opportunity cost than its trading partners.
 
• A comparative advantage gives a company the ability to sell goods and services at a lower price than its competitors and realize stronger sales margins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Adam Smith was a Scottish economist also known as the Father of economics or the Father of Capitalism.
 
• Amartya Sen is a world-renowned economist awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize.
 
 
• He has propounded "the concept of public welfare economics".
 
 
 
• Good Economics for a Hard Time was written by Abhijit V Banerjee and Esther Duflo.
 
 
• In this book Nobel laureates Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo debunk myths about migration.

questions.question: Which law of Newton provides a quantitative definition of force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second law of motion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Newton’s Second Law:
 
• The rate of change in linear momentum of a body is directly proportional to the external force applied to the body and this change takes place always in the direction of the applied force.
 
• If a body of mass m moves with velocity vec v then its linear momentum can be given by vec p = mv and if force vec F is applied to a body, then
 
• therefore vec F = m a
 
• Where F = Force, m = mass and a = acceleration
 
• From the above concept, it is clear that **Newton's ****Second law of motion** provides the definition of force.
 
• **The correct option is 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Newton’s First law:

 
 
• A body continues to be in its state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line unless it is acted upon by some external force to change the state.
 
• If no net force acts on a body, then the velocity of the body cannot change i.e. the body cannot accelerate.
 
• Newton’s first law defines inertia and is rightly called the law of inertia.
 
 
 
• Newton’s Third Law:
 
 
• To every action, there is always an equal (in magnitude) and opposite (in direction) reaction.
 
• When a body exerts a force on any other body, the second body also exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.
 
• Forces in nature always occur in pairs. A single isolated force is not possible.
 
 
 
• **The universal law of gravitation:**
 
 
• The universal law of gravitation was propounded by Sir Isaac Newton.
 
• Newton used the universal law of gravity to prove that the moon is accelerating towards Earth just as a body on Earth is falling towards Earth.
 
• According to the Universal law of gravitation, the force between two bodies is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to a square of the distance.
 
• The law was given in the year 1687.

questions.question: The Deomali is the highest mountain peak of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Odisha.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deomali (1672m) mountain peak is situated on the Eastern Ghat in Odisha.

questions.question: Ozone is an allotrope of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen.**

 
• Ozone also is known as Trioxygen which is a triatomic molecule consisting of three oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16b75fb2f33f4f17a94db40f4e1c304278c9d1ca9095caf14d95c6ef137d94ec.png] 

 
• Oxygen is insoluble in acidic pyrogallol. 
 
• Oxygen is denser than air. 
 
• Ozone is created by the action of daylight on oxygen.
 
• Ozone at a ground level is considered a pollutant.

questions.question: Which of the following environment events is observed by switching off all lights at homes, business establishments, landmarks and so on for an hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth Hour.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth Hour is switching off the moment observed worldwide on the last Saturday of March every year.
 
• This environment event is observed by switching off all lights at homes, business establishments, landmarks and so on for an hour.
 
• It was first observed in 2007 by the World Wildlife Fund in Sydney.
 
• People switch off the lights of their premises for an hour at 8:30 pm (according to their local time) on the last Saturday of March.
 
• It is a symbolic action that connects with people and draws their attention to the climate crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• World Environment Day was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972 on the first day of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment.

 
 
• World Environment Day is celebrated on the 5th of June of every year.
 
 
 
• Earth Day Network (EDN), the organization that leads Earth Day worldwide, has chosen the theme of Earth Day-2018, "End Plastic Pollution".
 
 
• Earth Day is an annual event held on 22 April to demonstrate support for environmental protection. 
 
• Earth Day is observed on April 22 since 1970.
